limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.
rule: Two maroon (9) endpoints sit outside a cyan (8) wall lattice. Cyan cells that are 4-adjacent to an orange (7) cell are unusable. Recolour to maroon the legal route between the endpoints with the fewest steps, breaking ties by fewest direction changes. Turns on the endpoint legs count; the first move is not a turn.
scope: Constructed cyan lattices with gaps, orange exclusion zones and two exterior endpoints. Output is the unique route minimizing steps then direction changes. Default dimensions 7–21; explicit requested dimensions 7–30, and 1–4 oranges. Four original pairs reconstructed exactly.
constraints: Independent BFS shortest-step DAG plus turn-count dynamic programming agrees on 1700 cases (1698 distinct), including every 576 size pair in 7..30, all four orange counts at 7x7 and 30x30
Default 1000 samples: 874 obstruction-sensitive routes and 515 cases with multiple shortest routes resolved by turns; longest audited route 95 steps
Critic claim that 7x7 with four oranges is infeasible is disproved by executable examples; all requested counts preserved without generator narrowing
19 critic successful cases, eight deliberate rejections, plus 13 malformed controls; Python and numpy booleans rejected as integer controls
Maximum observed generation time 0.604 seconds across targeted size checks; no 1500-attempt exhaustion in this audit
known_limitations: Fewest-turn convention is required by the original test and archived solver but not isolated by the training examples; generated episodes should include demonstrations exercising it
Native oranges do not occupy wall intersections or touch each other; whole boundary segments remain. Explicit replay supports wider geometry
Cyan fragments outside the solution route may remain; 19/1000 default scenes contain isolated cyan cells
Detour and turn-tiebreak preferences are soft and relax after 1000 attempts; uniqueness and requested controls never relax
Output computed by constrained graph search over the constructed latent lattice, not a sampled reference input or imported reference transform

authored_scope: Random mode samples several things: wall row and column counts and spacing (gaps of 2-4 cells), margins of 1-2 cells, deleted internal segments, single-cell gaps, 1-4 oranges (on a wall or in a chamber, never on an intersection), and the endpoint pair on the outer boundary. Default sides are 7-21. A requested width or height may be 7-30. Sizes other than 9x7 and 9x9, more than four walls per axis, and more than two oranges are synthetic extensions beyond the fixtures. Explicit mode reconstructs fully specified scenes from latent walls, removed cells, oranges and endpoints. Explicit mode allows sides of 1-30 and oranges on intersections. Partial controls are not supported: fixed walls with random oranges or endpoints are rejected rather than mixed.
authored_constraints: Exactly two maroon endpoints. Each lies outside the lattice bounding box and is 4-adjacent to a cyan lattice cell.
Oranges lie strictly inside the lattice bounding box, are mutually non-adjacent in random mode, and each borders at least one cyan cell.
The optimal (steps, turns) route is unique, so heap-order tie-breaking never decides the output.
The route recolours at least one cyan cell (random mode requires at least two). There are no identity pairs.
The only input-to-output change is 8 to 9 along the route.
Isolated cyan leftovers are removed so no stray lattice fragments remain.
Sizes, coordinates and num_oranges must be exact integers. Bool, float and str are rejected.
